``` ::: ::: ## ### `slice_min(.data, order_by, n)` select rows with n smallest values of a variable ### `slice_max(.data, order_by, n)` select rows with n largest values of a variable ## Continuing storms example ::: panel-tabset ### `slice_max` Extracting storms with 3 highest wind speeds ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} slice_max(storms, wind, n = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 13 name year month day hour lat long status category wind pressure 1 Allen 1980 8 7 18 21.8 -86.4 hurricane 5 165 899 2 Gilbert 1988 9 14 0 19.7 -83.8 hurricane 5 160 888 3 Wilma 2005 10 19 12 17.3 -82.8 hurricane 5 160 882 4 Dorian 2019 9 1 16 26.5 -77 hurricane 5 160 910 5 Dorian 2019 9 1 18 26.5 -77.1 hurricane 5 160 910 # ℹ 2 more variables: tropicalstorm_force_diameter , # hurricane_force_diameter ``` ::: ::: ### `slice_min` Extracting storms with the lowest wind speed ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} slice_min(storms, wind, n = 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 61 × 13 name year month day hour lat long status category wind pressure 1 Bonnie 1986 6 28 6 36.5 -91.3 tropica… NA 10 1013 2 Bonnie 1986 6 28 12 37.2 -90 tropica… NA 10 1012 3 Charley 1986 8 13 12 30.1 -84 subtrop… NA 10 1009 4 Charley 1986 8 13 18 30.8 -84 subtrop… NA 10 1012 5 Charley 1986 8 14 0 31.4 -83.6 subtrop… NA 10 1013 6 Charley 1986 8 14 6 32 -83.1 subtrop… NA 10 1014 7 Charley 1986 8 14 12 32.5 -82.5 subtrop… NA 10 1015 8 Charley 1986 8 14 18 32.4 -82 subtrop… NA 10 1015 9 AL031987 1987 8 16 18 30.9 -83.2 tropica… NA 10 1014 10 AL031987 1987 8 17 0 31.4 -82.9 tropica… NA 10 1015 # ℹ 51 more rows # ℹ 2 more variables: tropicalstorm_force_diameter , # hurricane_force_diameter ``` ::: ::: ::: ## {background-image="../img/horst_dplyr_mutate.png" background-size="70%"} ## Translating wind speed to km/hour Most of the world uses kilometers instead of miles. We can calculate km/hr by using: $$\text{kmh} = 1.60934 \times \text{mph}$$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} storms <- mutate(storms, wind_kmh = 1.60934 * wind) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} select(storms, wind, wind_kmh) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 19,537 × 2 wind wind_kmh 1 25 40.2 2 25 40.2 3 25 40.2 4 25 40.2 5 25 40.2 6 25 40.2 7 25 40.2 8 30 48.3 9 35 56.3 10 40 64.4 # ℹ 19,527 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Try it ::: task Create a new column in `flights` giving the *average speed* of the flight while it was in the air. What are the units of this variable? Make the variable in terms of miles per hour. ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## {background-image="../img/horst_dplyr_case_when.png" background-size="90%"} ## Example The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) considers a flight to be delayed when it is 15 minutes later than its scheduled time. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights <- mutate( flights, delayed = case_when( dep_delay >= 15 ~ "Delayed", dep_delay < 15 ~ "On time", .default = "other") ) ``` ::: ## Your turn ::: {.task .nonincremental .smaller} Suppose that you don't think the FAA gives enough information in their definition of a delayed flight, so you come up with the following delay categories: - `dep_delay <= 0` -\> none - `dep_delay` between 1 and 15 minutes -\> minimal - `dep_delay` between 16 and 30 minutes -\> delayed - `dep_delay` between 31 and 60 minutes -\> major - `dep_delay` over 60 minutes -\> extreme Use `mutate()` and `case_when()` to create a `delay_category` variable in the `flights` data frame. ::: # `%>% or |>` {.maize} ## {.center} ::::: columns ::: {.column .nonincremental width="60%"} - "dataframe first, dataframe once" - Combine multiple operations with the pipe - Think "and then" when reading code ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ![](../img/magittr-pipe.png){fig-align="right"} ::: ::::: ## Using `%>%` or `|>` - `%>%` or `|>` passes result on left into first argument of function on right - *Chaining* functions together lets you read Left-to-right, top-to-bottom ## Using `%>% or |>` ### `filter()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} filter(storms, status == "hurricane") ``` ::: becomes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} storms %>% filter(status == "hurricane") ``` ::: ::: {.fragment} ### `arrange()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} arrange(storms, wind) ``` ::: becomes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} storms |> arrange(wind) ``` ::: ::: ## Using `%>%` or `|>` We can also build up a series of pipes. We're interested in the storms with the *lowest* wind speed *that were still classified as hurricanes*. ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1|2|3"} storms %>% filter(status == "hurricane") %>% arrange(wind) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4,803 × 14 name year month day hour lat long status category wind pressure 1 Blanche 1975 7 27 6 35.9 -70 hurrica… 1 65 987 2 Caroline 1975 8 30 0 23.3 -94.2 hurrica… 1 65 990 3 Caroline 1975 8 30 6 23.5 -94.9 hurrica… 1 65 990 4 Caroline 1975 8 30 12 23.7 -95.6 hurrica… 1 65 989 5 Doris 1975 8 31 0 34.9 -46.3 hurrica… 1 65 990 6 Doris 1975 8 31 6 34.8 -45.7 hurrica… 1 65 990 7 Eloise 1975 9 16 18 19.5 -68.4 hurrica… 1 65 1002 8 Eloise 1975 9 17 0 19.6 -69.2 hurrica… 1 65 997 9 Eloise 1975 9 22 6 24.8 -89.4 hurrica… 1 65 993 10 Faye 1975 9 26 0 26.5 -60 hurrica… 1 65 990 # ℹ 4,793 more rows # ℹ 3 more variables: tropicalstorm_force_diameter , # hurricane_force_diameter , wind_kmh ``` ::: ::: ## Using `%>%` or `|>` We're interested in the storms with the *lowest* wind speed *that were still classified as hurricanes*, *that reached category 2*. ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1|2|3|4"} storms %>% filter(status == "hurricane") %>% filter(category > 1) %>% arrange(wind) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2,255 × 14 name year month day hour lat long status category wind pressure 1 Eloise 1975 9 22 18 26.5 -89.4 hurricane 2 85 980 2 Faye 1975 9 26 18 31 -63.1 hurricane 2 85 985 3 Faye 1975 9 28 0 38.4 -63.7 hurricane 2 85 985 4 Gladys 1975 10 3 6 43.7 -57 hurricane 2 85 960 5 Gladys 1975 10 3 12 46.6 -50.6 hurricane 2 85 960 6 Emmy 1976 8 26 18 27.7 -54.8 hurricane 2 85 976 7 Emmy 1976 8 27 12 30.9 -53.7 hurricane 2 85 975 8 Emmy 1976 8 28 12 33.5 -56.6 hurricane 2 85 975 9 Emmy 1976 8 31 12 35.1 -44.9 hurricane 2 85 977 10 Gloria 1976 9 30 6 32.2 -59.8 hurricane 2 85 971 # ℹ 2,245 more rows # ℹ 3 more variables: tropicalstorm_force_diameter , # hurricane_force_diameter , wind_kmh ``` ::: ::: ## Combining with `ggplot` Pipes become especially useful when we combine them with `ggplot()`: ::: {.cell output-location='column-fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-3|4|4-9"} storms |> filter(status == "hurricane") |> filter(category > 1) |> ggplot(aes(x = wind, y = hurricane_force_diameter)) + geom_jitter() + labs( title = "Force diameter vs wind speed", subtitle = "Hurricanes only" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](slides07_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-30-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Your turn ::: {.task .nonincremental} *Chain* the last two parts together, so that the resulting dataset contains both `avg_speed` and `delay_category`. Pipe this new dataset into `ggplot()` to answer the question "is there a relationship between average speed and how late a flight is delayed?" If you have time, create a new graph which only contains *flights to MSP*. ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
